rows.title: The address book record carries the address's type and what it can be used for
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 asks what type of address is being added and what it can be used for, and Sam's 9 October ruling keeps both answers because a question the service asks must persist and DR1 asked for address pickers filtered by role (c-176). Today the address-book record is untyped and its API carries no type or use, so nothing can keep those answers, and the address book list's type tabs and the DR1 role-filtered pickers have nothing to filter on. Afterwards an API caller can create, read and update an address with its type and uses, in a field shape the address-book service designs in its own conventions, and addresses saved before the change still read back.
acceptanceCriteria: Creating an address through the address book API with its address type and one or more uses (place of origin, consignor, place of destination, consignee, importer, branch address) stores them, and reading the address back by id returns the same type and the same uses (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-079; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-081; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-137; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-115, p1-116)
Updating an address through the API with a different set of uses replaces its uses with the new set, and the read-back shows the new set (repo:addressbook p2-071; prototype:dr2-1-source p16-079)

A create or update carrying a use outside those six is refused with a 400 validation problem whose errors name the uses, and nothing is saved (repo:addressbook p1-039, p1-045; ruling:sam-2026-10-07 p1-010)
An address created without a type or uses, and every address saved before this change, is still accepted and reads back with no type and no uses (repo:addressbook p1-001, p1-003)

The address book's locked API contract describes the type and uses on the create and update requests and on the read response, with the six allowed uses (repo:addressbook p2-097, p2-098; document:dr1-parity-backlog p7-064, p7-065)
rows.gate: Check the type and uses field names, the six use values and how a record without them reads back in the locked contract, before the add form, the address book list's type tabs and the DR1 address pickers build on it.
rows.notes: Pass 1 slice on its own: the typed record is the foundation the add form's uses question, the list's type tabs (address-book-list area) and DR1 inc-047/inc-048 rest on, so it lands first and gates. Observable through the API in every environment the tests repo's address book API client reaches (local stack and CDP). Rewritten for Sam's 9 October ruling: the record now carries the address's type as well as its uses (req-1256), the field names and shape are the address-book service's (c-176; ruling claims 66, 70, 116), so no criterion names the prototype's 'primary type' or 'address book type'. The old criterion that a stray 'type' or 'role' field is still refused is dropped: c-176 leaves that rejection for the service to keep or replace when it names its new fields. Type and uses stay optional on the API so a journey's handshake add and every existing record keep saving; the add form makes a use required outside a journey. Updates fully replace the editable fields today, so the edit page must post the stored type and uses back; that is the edit row's criterion. Decision: refuse an unknown use with a 400, because the record only means something with known values (validation clause of ruling:sam-2026-10-07).

rows.title: Address validation messages match Design Release 2.1, on the form and in the API
rows.detail: Four required-field messages change wording to match Design Release 2.1 and their field labels. The address book API's messages change with them, because the API's message reaches the user when the service rejects a save. Afterwards the add and edit forms, and the API's validation problem, give the new wording.
acceptanceCriteria: Saving the add or edit form without a name shows 'Enter a name or organisation name' inline and in the 'There is a problem' summary, and the address book API's blank-name validation message is 'Enter a name or organisation name' (prototype:dr2-1-source p15-071, p16-066; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-070, p16-114; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-129, p6-162; repo:addressbook p1-010)

Saving without a postcode shows 'Enter a postcode or Zip code', and the API's blank-postcode message is the same (prototype:dr2-1-source p15-074, p16-069; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-073; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-132; repo:addressbook p1-021)

Saving without a country, or with a country not in the list, shows 'Select a country', and the API's blank-country message is the same (prototype:dr2-1-source p15-075, p16-070; repo:insfrontend p3-055, p3-056; repo:addressbook p1-025, p2-023)

Saving without a phone number shows 'Enter a phone number', and the API's blank-phone message is the same (prototype:dr2-1-source p15-077, p16-072; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-075; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-134; repo:addressbook p1-028)
rows.notes: Unchanged by the 9 October ruling. Pass 1 had one slice per message; pass 2 combines them because each makes the same two edits (the form's copy and the API's message) on the same review and ladder. Kept apart from the record row because it carries no structural change and can land in parallel. The other required-field messages already match (exists). Today's length limits and email format check stay (req-1244, exists; c-179, which the germinal data fields' Standard Address Block confirms); whether phone gains a telephone-format check is a question (req-1869, c-256), not built here. Welsh drafts for the new strings are the Welsh row's.

rows.title: Adding an address starts by choosing its type
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 asks what kind of address is being added before any fields, because the type decides the form and the uses offered next. Today the address book's add is the address form itself. Afterwards 'Add a new address' on the address book opens a new 'Choose an address type' page, on a path of its own in the INS front door's path shape; choosing Origin or Consignor, Destination, Consignee or Importer, or Branch moves on to the address form, which stays where it is today (the page the animals frontend's handshake links to), retitled 'Add address and contact details' and able to go back to the type page. The chosen type is remembered while the add is in progress and cleared when it starts afresh or saves. Transporter is its own row.
acceptanceCriteria: From the address book list, 'Add a new address' opens a page with the caption 'Add a new address', the heading 'Choose an address type', a radio group whose legend repeats the heading visually hidden, and a 'Back' link to the address book list (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-001, p16-003, p16-004, p16-005, p16-013; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-038, p16-039; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-104, p6-105, p6-106, p6-112)

The options are, in order: 'Origin or Consignor' (hint 'Place of origin, Consignor'), 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' (hint 'Place of destination, Consignee, Importer'), 'Transporter' (hint 'Private, Commercial') and 'Branch' (hint 'Branch address'), with a 'Continue' button (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-006 to p16-010, p16-012; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-040 to p16-043; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-107 to p6-111, p6-113)

Continuing with no type chosen shows 'Select an address type' inline on the radios and in a 'There is a problem' summary whose link goes to the first option (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-016; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-045; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-114, p6-115)

Choosing 'Origin or Consignor', 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' or 'Branch' and continuing opens the address form, which posts back to itself and shows the caption 'Add new address', the heading 'Add address and contact details', no notification status banner, and a 'Back' link to 'Choose an address type' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-018, p16-019, p16-021, p16-022, p16-023, p16-024; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-047, p16-053, p16-069; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-116, p6-117, p6-118; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-090)
Opening the address form outside a notification journey with no address type chosen goes to 'Choose an address type' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-020)

Going back from the address form to 'Choose an address type' shows the chosen type selected; opening 'Add a new address' again from the address book starts with no type selected and empty fields, and after a save the next add starts empty (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-002, p16-011, p16-087)

The browser titles read 'Choose an address type - Import notification service - GOV.UK', 'Add address and contact details - Import notification service - GOV.UK', and on the edit page 'Edit address and contact details - Import notification service - GOV.UK', keeping the 'Error: ' prefix when a page shows errors (trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-038, p16-053, p16-107; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-104, p6-117, p6-158; trace:ins-fit p1-003, p3-003)
rows.gate: Check the two-step add and its in-progress state, which the add-details, manual-entry and transporter rows copy, and that a notification journey's handshake into the address form still opens it directly, without 'Choose an address type', and returns the new address id (c-106).
rows.notes: Rewritten for Sam's 9 October ruling (claims 72, 73, 75, 90): the address form stays at the address book's existing add path (the one the animals frontend's handshake links to) and the type step takes a new path in the INS front door's path shape, rather than moving the form to the prototype's /add/lookup; no criterion names a path. The previous open question on the handshake (journey mode) is settled by c-106: keep today's handshake, and in journey mode the form skips the type step; that behaviour is req-1284's row. Pass 1 slices combined: the type page, its error, its options, the hop to the address form and the form's caption, heading and back link all share one route pair and one review. The address form reuses today's fields at first; its content changes in the next rows. Title format: the suffix comes from the shared INS layout, which the address book list and the layout area also change; make the change once there. The k6 performance suite's add scenario posts to the address form with no type; whether it chooses a type first is req-1870, still a question, so no perftests change here. Welsh drafts are the Welsh row's.

rows.title: The add-details form for an address entered by hand
rows.detail: The address form's address and contact fields take Design Release 2.1's layout and copy: 'Address' and 'Contact details' section headings (also on the edit form), the 'Name or organisation' label, no County field, new widths, an alphabetical country list with United Kingdom pre-selected for Origin or Consignor and a 'Select one' placeholder, and cancel as a link under the button. Today the add form has 'Enter address details' and 'Enter contact details' headings, a County field, United Kingdom always first and a secondary cancel button.
acceptanceCriteria: On the add-details step and the edit page the address fields sit under the section heading 'Address' and Email address and Phone number under 'Contact details' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-038, p16-049, p15-062, p15-063; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-055, p16-062, p16-108; trace:ins-fit p1-008, p1-018, p3-005-m1)

On the add-details step the name field is labelled 'Name or organisation', while the edit page keeps 'Name or organisation name' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-039; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-056; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-121, p6-161-m1)
The add-details step has no County field (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-045; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-054)

On the add-details step 'Name or organisation', both address lines and 'Email address' are full width, 'Town or city' and 'Postcode or Zip code' half width, and 'Phone number' two-thirds width (trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-059, p16-060, p16-064-m1)

On the add and edit forms the Country select lists reference data's countries in alphabetical order, with United Kingdom in its alphabetical place (prototype:dr2-1-source p15-065; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-110; c-177)
For 'Origin or Consignor' the Country select opens with United Kingdom selected, and its blank first option reads 'Select one' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-047-m1; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-078)

Below 'Save and continue' the add-details step has a 'Cancel and return to address book' link, not a button, that goes to the address book and saves nothing (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-065; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-068, p16-134)
rows.notes: Depends on 'Adding an address starts by choosing its type' (the add-details step it changes). Pass 1 slices combined: section headings, label, County, widths, country order and default, placeholder and cancel are all copy and layout on the same form and review together. The section headings and the alphabetical country order are asserted on both forms because each requirement says 'add and edit'; the edit page's own order, widths and placeholder are the edit row's. What the country list holds is reference data's unfiltered list, MDM's content (c-177, req-1235 exists); nothing here waits on MDM. In journey mode the cancel stays the journey's own (req-1284's row), so this row's cancel link is the address book add's.

rows.title: Saving a new address with its uses
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 asks what an address can be used for on the add-details step and saves the ticked uses with it, then shows the user the new address among its kind. Afterwards an Origin or Consignor address offers 'Place of origin' and 'Consignor' after a section break, a use is required once the fields are valid, the save stores the address's type and ticked uses in the address book, and the user lands on the address book list showing that type, with the new address first, a reworded success banner, its full address and searchable by its uses.
acceptanceCriteria: For 'Origin or Consignor' the address and contact fields show straight away with no address search, then a section break, then the uses question with the legend 'What can this address be used for?', the hint 'Select where this address can be used' and the checkboxes 'Place of origin' and 'Consignor', with no hint on either option (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-025, p16-048, p16-052, p16-053, p16-054, p16-055; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-054, p16-065, p16-066; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-119, p6-120)

With the address and contact fields valid and no use ticked, saving shows 'Select what this address can be used for' inline and in the error summary, linked to the first use option; while any field is invalid the uses are not checked (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-076; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-077, p16-129; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-135)

Saving stores the address in the address book with its type and every ticked use, and a use posted that does not belong to the chosen type is not stored (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-078, p16-079; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-056-m1, p16-081)

After saving an Origin or Consignor address the user lands on the address book list showing Origin or Consignor addresses, with the new address listed first and a 'View' link to its own page (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-083, p16-086; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-079, p16-081, p16-082; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-137, p6-139; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-075, p1-091)
The list then shows a 'Success' banner reading '<name> address added to your address book' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-085; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-080)

The added address reads as address line 1, address line 2, town or city, county and postcode joined by commas, leaving out blanks, with the country shown separately (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-080, p15-084; trace:ins-fit p1-058)
The added address is found by the address book search on its name, on a use such as 'Consignor', on part of its address and on its country (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-082)
rows.notes: Depends on the rows 'The address book record carries the address's type and what it can be used for', 'Adding an address starts by choosing its type' and 'The add-details form for an address entered by hand'. Cross-area: the landing view needs the address book list's type tabs, and the search on a use needs the list's search over uses (address-book-list area), so this row depends on the list rows that build them (inc-067, inc-069 today). Rewritten for Sam's 9 October ruling: the list's tab parameter, its values and the uses field name are the INS service's to name (claims 66, 91), so no criterion names a query string. The INS frontend's address book client and its stub-mode stub must carry the type and uses. The banner's no-name fallback ('Address added to your address book') cannot be reached in any environment, since a name is required on the form and the API; it is listed as unobservable. In journey mode the add ticks the role's use and returns to the journey with no address book banner; that is req-1284's row, and a journey-mode save must keep working here. Pass 1 slices combined: the uses question, its validation, the save and the return all exercise one save and one review.

rows.title: Destination, Consignee or Importer and Branch addresses entered by hand, with a fixed UK country
rows.detail: Destination, consignee, importer and branch addresses are in the UK. Design Release 2.1 finds them by search first, but Sam's 9 October ruling blocks address search until the address lookup is a real feature and has manual entry built now (c-217). Afterwards, in every environment, the add-details step for these two types opens with the address and contact fields and the uses question shown and no search box, as 'Origin or Consignor' does; the country is fixed to United Kingdom; the uses question is headed 'Address type' with each type's uses; and a save lands on the address book list showing that type.
acceptanceCriteria: For 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch' the add-details step opens with the address fields, contact fields and uses question shown and no address search, in the fit suites, on the local stack and in every CDP environment (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-178, p1-182; prototype:dr2-1-source p16-036; c-217)

For these two types the Country select holds only 'United Kingdom', pre-selected, and the saved address's country is United Kingdom whatever country is posted (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-046; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-090)

For these two types the uses question's legend is 'Address type', with the hint 'Select where this address can be used' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-052, p16-053; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-095, p16-099)

A 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' address offers the use checkboxes 'Place of destination', 'Consignee' and 'Importer' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-056; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-097; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-144)
A 'Branch' address offers exactly one use checkbox, 'Branch address' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-057; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-099; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-147)

Every field, error message and the uses check on these two types are the same as for 'Origin or Consignor', and a save stores the address with its type and ticked uses (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-182; prototype:dr2-1-source p16-076, p16-078)

A saved Destination, Consignee or Importer address lands the user on the address book list showing Destination, Consignee or Importer addresses, and a Branch address on the list showing Branch addresses, each listed first (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-083; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-139; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-075, p1-091)
rows.notes: Depends on 'Saving a new address with its uses' (the uses question, its validation and the save it extends) and on 'The add-details form for an address entered by hand'. Rewritten for Sam's 9 October ruling (claims 178 to 182, c-217): the search-first layout (req-1214) and its error reveal (req-1285) moved to the blocked address search row; this row is the manual entry the ruling builds now, so the per-environment search setting the earlier draft introduced, and its gate, are gone. req-1862 states exactly this manual-entry behaviour and areas.json gives it to no area, so this draft covers it (decision: it belongs on this page's row; combiner, keep it here rather than drafting another row). The 'Enter address manually' control (req-652's, in the journey pages' row) is not needed while no search shows. The landing criterion restates req-1259 (in 'Saving a new address with its uses') for these two types and needs the list area's type tabs.

rows.title: The address search finds UK addresses as you type, once the address lookup is real
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1 opens Destination, Consignee or Importer and Branch addresses on a free-text type-ahead search that fills the address from a picked result, with manual entry as the way round it. Its results must be real UK addresses from the address lookup the INS backend serves (c-178). Sam's 9 October ruling blocks all of it until the address lookup becomes a real feature of the INS front door and INS backend: today only the EUDPA-390 spike exists, gated to dev and local on a standalone page. When it lands this area is re-distilled and this row rewritten to what search then needs, including which environments it runs in.
acceptanceCriteria: For 'Destination, Consignee or Importer' and 'Branch' the add-details step opens with only the address search; the address fields, contact fields and uses question stay hidden until an address is picked or manual entry is chosen, and open already revealed when an address or address line 1 is already present (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-025, p16-037; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-083, p16-096, p16-098; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-140, p6-141)

Typing in the address search lists matching addresses below it in a list labelled 'Address search results', each shown as the lookup's formatted address line with the typed text in bold, and a screen-reader announcement gives the number of results, such as '1 result available' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-027, p16-029, p16-030; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-086, p16-086-m1; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-143; c-178)

Picking a result hides the search, announces the selection to screen readers and reveals the fields filled from it: premises to address line 1, street and locality to address line 2, town to town or city, the postcode, and country United Kingdom; name, email address and phone number stay blank, and anything the user types over a filled field is what is saved (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-033, p16-034, p16-035; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-087, p16-088, p16-089; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-145; repo:insfrontend p5-052 to p5-059; c-178)

The search finds real UK addresses from the INS backend's address lookup, and when the lookup fails or finds nothing no results are listed and the address can still be entered and saved by hand (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-028; repo:insfrontend p5-067, p5-070, p5-071; c-178)

Saving the search layout with nothing picked or typed shows the six field errors with the address and contact fields revealed, so each error summary link moves to a visible field; the errors stay until the next save, and the typed values, ticked uses and search text are kept (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-077; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-092, p16-094; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-142; repo:insfrontend p3-065; c-180)
openQuestions: Blocked (ruling:sam-2026-10-09 claims 178 to 184; c-217): the INS front door and INS backend team must make the address lookup a real feature (today only the EUDPA-390 spike, gated to dev and local on a standalone page and not wired in). Once it lands, re-distil this area: which environments the search runs in, what else it needs, and these criteria per environment are settled then.
rows.notes: Rewritten for Sam's 9 October ruling: the search row and the search parts of the previous 'Destination, Consignee or Importer and Branch' row (req-1214, req-1285) stay in the backlog, blocked on the lookup, so the manual-entry row can build now. The earlier default (stub locally, real lookup in CDP dev, off elsewhere) is replaced by the ruling, so the per-environment criteria are gone until the re-distil. The lookup returns no organisation name, so the screen-reader announcement names the picked address (c-178). The spike page itself stays as it is (out of scope). The Welsh for the search's strings is this row's own, since the Welsh sweep row no longer waits for it.

rows.title: Editing an address matches Design Release 2.1
rows.detail: The edit page takes Design Release 2.1's heading, field order, layout and country select, returns the user to where they came from on Back and Cancel, keeps the address's type and every use it has, words its success banner as Design Release 2.1 does, and sends the user back rather than to an error page for an address not in their book. Today the heading is 'Edit address details', Phone comes before Email, the fields use other widths, the country select keeps a placeholder, Back and Cancel ignore any return path, and unknown ids show page not found.
acceptanceCriteria: The edit page's heading and page title are 'Edit address and contact details', with no caption (prototype:dr2-1-source p15-057; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-107; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-158, p6-159)

On the edit page 'Email address' comes before 'Phone number', and the fields use the add form's section headings, order and widths, keeping 'County (optional)' between 'Town or city' and 'Postcode or Zip code' (prototype:dr2-1-source p15-063; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-108; trace:ins-fit p3-005-m1, p3-007-m1)
On the edit page the Country select has no blank placeholder option and shows the stored country selected (prototype:dr2-1-source p15-065; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-110; trace:ins-fit p3-013)

The edit page's 'Back' link goes to the page the edit was opened from when one was given, otherwise to the address's view page (prototype:dr2-1-source p15-058; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-113; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-092)
'Cancel' on the edit page saves nothing, clears any errors and goes to the page the edit was opened from, by default the address's view page (prototype:dr2-1-source p15-067, p15-068)

The edit page shows no type or uses, and an address saved with several uses still has its type and all of them after an edit through the edit page (prototype:dr2-1-source p15-061; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-111; c-181)

After a valid edit the list shows a 'Success' banner reading '<Name> address updated', the name with its first letter capitalised and the rest lower case, for example 'Green valley farm address updated' for 'GREEN VALLEY FARM' (prototype:dr2-1-source p15-083; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-116; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-164)

Opening or saving the edit page for an address that is not in the user's address book (unknown, another organisation's, deleted or a malformed id) goes to the page the edit was opened from, or the address book list, saving nothing (prototype:dr2-1-source p15-056, p15-069; repo:insfrontend p3-080, p3-081, p3-093)
rows.notes: Depends on 'The address book record carries the address's type and what it can be used for' (the kept type and uses: an update fully replaces the editable fields, so the edit must post the stored type and uses back) and on 'The add-details form for an address entered by hand' (the section headings and country order it shares). Sam's 9 October ruling: the return parameter's name is the service's and its allow-list stays (claim 92), so the criteria say where Back and Cancel go, not how the return is carried. A valid edit still returns to the list's default view (exists). The banner's no-name fallback ('Address updated') cannot be reached in any environment, since a name is required; it is listed as unobservable. The edit page's Cache-Control is left as it is (out of scope). Pass 1 slices combined: every criterion is on the one edit page and its save.

rows.title: Choosing Transporter on the address book's add hands over to adding a transporter
rows.detail: Design Release 2.1's 'Choose an address type' offers Transporter, but a transporter is not an address-book address: choosing it leaves the address book add for the add-a-transporter pages, wherever the real services keep transporter records and their pages (ruling 9 October, claim 93). Reached this way, those pages say so and lead back to 'Choose an address type'. The existing row this sits in also holds the transporter area's back, cancel and save from the address book (req-461 to req-463); this draft covers only this area's hand-over.
acceptanceCriteria: On the compose stack and in CDP, choosing 'Transporter' on 'Choose an address type' and continuing leaves the address book add and opens the add-a-transporter page; reached this way, its 'Back' link returns to 'Choose an address type' (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-017; trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-048, p16-052; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-148; ruling:sam-2026-10-09 p1-093)
That page shows the caption 'Add a new transporter' and the heading and page title 'Choose a transporter type' (trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-049; prototype:dr2-1-specs p6-148)
That page shows the warning 'Check the transporter list before adding new transporters to avoid duplicates.' (trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-050)

That page offers the radios 'Private transporter' and 'Commercial', the latter with the hint 'This can only be a commercial transporter from Northern Ireland.', and a 'Continue' button (trace:prototype-dr2-1 p16-051, p16-051-m1)
rows.notes: Combiner: merge into inc-074 with the transporters area's draft (req-461, req-462, req-463), as the backlog already does: one route from the address book's type page through the add-a-transporter pages and back. rows.title: A notification journey's add keeps today's handshake and opens Design Release 2.1's add page in journey mode
rows.detail: Where the journey's add-address page lives is cross-service behaviour the prototype cannot express, so the INS frontend stays the address book's only writer and a journey's 'Add a new address' keeps handing over through today's handshake (c-106). In journey mode the INS add page shows Design Release 2.1's add page: it skips 'Choose an address type', opens the add-details step for the type the role implies with the role's use ticked, and returns to the journey page each button names, with no address book banner. The existing row this sits in also holds the journey area's buttons, landings and banner (req-637 and others); this draft covers this area's journey-mode entry.
acceptanceCriteria: On the compose stack and in CDP, 'Add a new address' on a notification's party page still hands over to the INS address book's add page through today's handshake, for the registered live-animals journey only, with the return built on the server (repo:insfrontend p3-095 to p3-107; trace:e2e p15-006, p15-007; c-106)

Reached by the handshake, the INS add page does not ask 'Choose an address type' and opens 'Add address and contact details' for the type the role implies, with that role's use ticked (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-088, p16-091; c-106)

'Save and select' saves the address and lands on the notification's Consignment addresses page with it chosen for the role; 'Save and return to address page' saves it and lands on the role's picker with nothing chosen; 'Cancel and return to hub' saves nothing and lands on the notification's hub (prototype:dr2-1-source p16-092 to p16-095; repo:tests p5-034, p5-035, p5-036; c-106)

Landing back in the journey shows no address book banner, and the journey still refuses a return with an unknown fulfilment or a stale handshake token (repo:insfrontend p3-108 to p3-112, p3-138; trace:e2e p15-008, p15-009)

Germinal products: req-1831 (the germinal set's party pickers use the same handshake, with the INS address book accepting the germinal set and returning to its own address-return) is given to no area in areas.json; ruling 9 October claim 61 keeps it in the INS themes, proven in the ins Playwright project. It belongs beside this row but is not drafted here, since it is not in this area's requirements; the combiner drafts it, depending on this row.

rows.title: Welsh drafts for the new add and edit copy
rows.detail: The address book keeps English and Welsh copy side by side. Changing only the English would leave the Welsh describing the old pages. Afterwards every new or changed English string on the add and edit pages has a Welsh entry, still marked as an unreviewed machine draft.
acceptanceCriteria: The address book's Welsh copy has an entry for every new or changed English string on 'Choose an address type', the add-details step (every type's layout, the uses question and every error message) and the edit page, and no add or edit page shows an English string where the Welsh copy is in use (repo:insfrontend p3-113 to p3-120)
The Welsh copy stays marked as an unreviewed machine draft that must not ship to users without Welsh Language Standards sign-off (repo:insfrontend p3-113)
rows.notes: Depends on every todo row in this area that adds or changes English copy. It no longer waits for the address search row, which is blocked on the address lookup (ruling 9 October, claims 178 to 180); that row drafts its own Welsh when it is built. Kept as one sweep so the Welsh is checked once against the finished English; each earlier row may draft its Welsh as it goes, and this row then confirms nothing is missing.
